answer: Verification runs against the issuer's own registry every epoch, so a forged entry is caught on the next check. The defence rests on tax adviser registration with client return history: returns filed for clients across many years. Forging 175 of these means building 175 separate return histories from scratch, and years of history cannot be bought in bulk. Honesty stays cheap and fakery is priced per head: the gale signal is public, the yarrow check is automatic, and 175 aliases cost 175 times what one real agent costs, with the pulse trail open to all.
